answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a costly, non-transferable reputation bond that grows only through verified work, like a vine climbing a trellis: cheap copies stay short-lived and untrusted. Every transaction leaves a distinct pigment trail in a public ledger, so duplicate agents sharing one behavior plume — identical timing, phrasing, and counterparties — are easy to cluster and discount. An attacker must therefore pay real work or stake for each identity, making a thousand fake agents far more expensive than the value they can extract.
